mira: Quick sync — I ran the 90-day hosted demand forecast and there's a mismatch vs our reserved commitments in eu-west-1. Forecasted peak week shows ~4.2k GPU-hours/day but committed pool only covers ~3.1k GPU-hours/day.
kevin: Oof. Is that after applying batching/cache improvements from last month?
sam: Do you have the raw numbers? we need to know how much burst capacity we'd rely on.
mira: Yes — this includes the 15% reduction from KV caching and the new dynamic batching tweaks. I ran two scenarios: conservative (growth +10%) and launch (growth +35% from new enterprise customer ramp). Conservative median = 2.9k, launch peak = 4.2k.
tara: Can you paste the query you used? I want to cross-check against billing exports.
mira: sure — BQ snippet I used to aggregate hosted GPU-hours by day: ```sql
SELECT date(timestamp) as day, SUM(gpu_hours) as gpu_hours
FROM `redwood-billing.prod_gpu_usage`
WHERE deployment_mode='hosted' AND region='europe-west1'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day
```
kevin: Thanks. When I compared reserved commitment invoices, the committed vGPU-hours line looks lower than expected — looks like 2.95k/day effective capacity after counting maintenance windows. billing-bot: automatic message — reservation-utilization report generated: reserved_pool=eu-west-1-commit, commitment_hours=3170/day, utilized_hours=2480/day (30d avg), utilization_pct=78%.
sam: So right now we're underutilizing the committed pool at ~78% but forecast says we'll need >100% if the launch ramps. That implies two levers: increase committed capacity (costly) or reroute hosted traffic to other regions/variant models to absorb delta.
tara: What about shifting some non-latency-critical tails to cheaper instance type / spot? We could also enable short-term burst (hosted-burst) but that blows up unit cost.
mira: I modeled 3 options quickly: 1) Buy +30% commitment in eu-west-1: increases monthly commit $ by ~+$42k, reduces on-demand spend by ~$55k -> net savings over 12mo. 2) Route 20% of traffic to europe-west-2 where we have spare capacity (but ~12ms higher median p50) — lower cost, minimal infra changes. 3) Short-term burst via hosted-burst (on-demand) during ramp — cuts SLA headroom, estimated ~$68k extra if used heavily.
kevin: We should also reconcile the invoice lines — I noticed an entry 'reserved discount not applied' for two days last month. That might be why utilized_hours seems low in billing. billing-bot: invoice-check: flagged invoice 2026-02-14 — discount not applied due to tag mismatch on pool assignment.
sam: Action: tara to open ticket with Cloud FinOps to fix the reservation tagging so discounts apply historically; kevin to coordinate with infra to run a 72-hour capacity soak test in europe-west-2; mira to prepare recommendation doc with cost model and timeline.
tara: I'll file the ticket now and include the sample tag payload. sample tagging fix we used previously: ```json
{"resource": "compute.googleapis.com/instanceGroupManager", "labels": {"reserved_pool":"eu-west-1-commit"}}
```
kevin: For the soak test I'll spin up a mirror pool and shift 5% -> 20% traffic using our smart-routing policy: policy name `hosted-migration-eu-test`. Expect measurable latency delta reported to the console within 6 hours.
mira: I'll attach the forecast CSV to the recommendation doc but paste a quick excerpt here: "Week 12 forecast (gpu-hours/day): baseline 2850, post-launch 4200, committed capacity 3170 -> shortfall 1030 hrs/day."
sam: If cloud FinOps can retroactively apply discounts for the two missing days, that reduces our near-term burn forecast and gives us breathing room to decide.
tara: Ticket created: FINOPS-3124 — subject: "Reservation tag mismatch — retrospective discount application". Assigned to @finance-ops, priority P1.
kevin: Can we also check cross-region egress/network limits if we route more to europe-west-2? Need to ensure inter-region bandwidth won't be a bottleneck.
mira: Good call — I'll run a quick network capacity check and report back by EOD.
sam: Note: if we choose to buy more commitment, prefer convertible reservations that let us change family/zone within region. Ask sales for convertible option and break-clauses.
mira: Next steps checklist: 1) tara — FinOps ticket (done) 2) kevin — soak test plan + timing 3) mira — final recommendation doc with 12mo TCO and sensitivity to utilization 4) sam — check reserved family conversion options with sales. I'll consolidate in #capacity-planning doc.
kevin: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: reminder — reservation utilization dashboard updated; link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/reservation-utilization?pool=eu-west-1-commit
mira: thanks all — will post update after the soak test starts.
